name: LLM Prompter Prototype
description_text:
Note: This is an individual assignment

You will operationalize your team’s Agent Persona into a working LLM-based prototype (prompt + instructions + tool configuration) that delivers your Pitch value proposition, executes the Journey Map moments that matter, and supports the needs/constraints of your User Persona(s). This is not a generic chatbot. It is a purpose-built agent that can be tested, measured, and iterated.

Inputs You Must Use (from prior assignments)

You are required to directly incorporate the following artifacts into your prototype:

Working Backwards Pitch (problem, customer, promise, key differentiators, success criteria)

User Persona(s) (goals, constraints, behaviors, context of use, accessibility considerations)

Agent Persona (agent role, responsibilities, boundaries, decision style, tone, escalation rules)

What You Will Build

A prototype LLM agent configuration using one of the following:

Google Gemini 

ChatGPT (Custom GPT or structured prompt pack)

Claude Code (project + system prompt + test set)

Cursor (application prototype)

Kiro (or any equivalent “agent builder” tool your team can access)

Your prototype must demonstrate at least one end-to-end “happy path” from your journey map, plus failure handling for common edge cases.

To do this, use this tool I built to assist you:

https://agentmaker.perfectpixels.com/ 

Here’s a summary you can reuse as a handout, README section, or internal doc.

Agent Behavior Maker — summary

What the tool does

Agent Behavior Maker is a workflow tool for designing and stress-testing how an LLM-powered agent should behave for a specific product. You feed in structured inputs about the product, the end user, and the agent you want to build. The app uses AWS Bedrock (Claude) to:

Extract structured insights from your documents (product, persona, agent framework).

Generate multiple conversation scenarios that fit your domain.

Simulate multi-turn chats between PersonaUser (your user) and AgentLLM (your agent).

Let you tune behavior with controls (tone, formality, verbosity, empathy, proactivity, creativity, technical depth) and regenerate the simulated conversation so you can see the effect.

Optionally continue the simulation by typing your own messages (user interrupt).

Export downloadable artifacts that encode what you learned.

It does not replace production deployment; it helps you iterate on persona and steering before you wire them into your real system.

What the output is

Output
Description

On screen
Scenarios (clickable cards) and simulated conversations (alternating user/agent messages) that reflect your documents and current control settings.

Export
A ZIP file with two Markdown files: updated-persona.md — persona-oriented summary (demographics, goals, pain points, product context, interaction preferences derived from your tested conversations and current sliders). ai-persona-steering.md — steering-style doc (identity, behavior rules mapped from controls, example dialogue snippet, export metadata).

Use the steering file as a starting point for system prompts, internal guidelines, or handoff to engineering.

Step-by-step instructions

Open the app (e.g. hosted URL or local dev).

Phase A — Submit materials

Provide three inputs: Product proposal (Who / What / Why / How style is fine), Your User persona, and Agent framework docs

You can paste text, upload .txt, or use a Google Doc URL (if supported in your build).

Optional: Try Demo — Museum Tour Guide loads sample content so you can explore the flow without writing docs from scratch.

Click Generate Scenarios and wait for processing to finish.

Phase B — Conversation playground

The tool will analyze your docs and build sample scenarios. Review suggested scenarios and click one to generate a simulated five-turn conversation. 

Review the PersonaUser / AgentLLM exchange

Optional: type a custom user message and send it to extend the thread (within limits).

Phase C — Agent controls

After documents are submitted, adjust Tone (dropdown) and the dials (formality, verbosity, empathy, proactivity, creativity, technical).

When you change controls, the app debounces and refreshes the latest simulated conversation so behavior tracks your settings.

Change documents or controls, regenerate scenarios or conversations, and export again as needed.

Export

Click Export Framework when you’re satisfied.

Save the ZIP and open the two .md files for persona and steering content.

Load the md as steering content into your LLM tool development tool of choice from above. Instruct it to create a chat bot using your outputted steering doc, and tweak as necessary to improve context and outcomes.

Once you are happy, screen record the interaction with Quicktime or other application.

lecture_alignment.definition: Designing systems and processes that automate repetitive tasks, reduce manual effort, and improve efficiency through intelligent orchestration.
Evaluative research method where representative users attempt tasks with a product to identify usability issues and measure performance.
Creating interactive representations of designs at varying levels of fidelity to test concepts, gather feedback, and communicate ideas.
Visual representations of user experiences over time, showing touchpoints, emotions, pain points, and opportunities across the customer journey.
Designing products that are usable by people with diverse abilities, following WCAG guidelines and inclusive design principles.
